subject.title: fix(telegram): DM lane stays dead after a wedged handler keeps it guarded; escalate to a supervised gateway restart

question: Should a channel report an unrecoverable in-process wedge through the shared ChannelAccountSnapshot.processRestartRequired contract, or should Telegram use a narrower injected gateway-restart request seam?
rationale: Both designs can preserve the no-double-processing invariant, but the shared field creates a permanent cross-channel plugin contract whose ownership and lifecycle semantics cannot be selected from implementation evidence alone.

options.title: Keep the generic health signal
options.body: Retain the optional snapshot field as a documented cross-channel contract after fixing the unmanaged hard-boundary behavior and covering its lifecycle semantics.

options.title: Use a Telegram-owned request seam
options.body: Replace the snapshot field with a narrowly injected restart-request capability owned by the Telegram runtime and gateway orchestration.

options.title: Pause gateway escalation
options.body: Leave the guarded-lane diagnostics in place but defer automatic gateway restart behavior until a permanent lifecycle contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Keep the generic health signal
recommendation.body: Retain the optional snapshot field as a documented cross-channel contract after fixing the unmanaged hard-boundary behavior and covering its lifecycle semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the Telegram polling and isolated-ingress lifecycle, and the existing review discussion already routes this exact contract decision to them.
